title: Smectic Superconductivity
abstract: We identify a mechanism in which soft nonunitary fluctuations of the pair condensate can suppress phase coherence in a two-dimensional Rashba superconductor proximate to easy-plane ferromagnetic order. This spin polarization couples linearly to the supercurrent through a Lifshitz invariant, acting as an emergent gauge field for the superconducting $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase. Integrating out soft magnetic fluctuations renormalizes the effective superfluid stiffness and drives the system into a "smectic" superconducting state, characterized by a finite-momentum helical phase texture and a long-wavelength stiffness that vanishes in one direction. Consequently, vortices no longer have a logarithmically divergent energy cost, and the quasi-long-range superconducting order is destroyed at any finite temperature. Weak lattice anisotropy pins the ferromagnetic order, cutting off the smectic-like behaviour at long wavelengths and thereby restoring a finite effective stiffness. Nonetheless, near the onset of magnetic order, the enhanced magnetic susceptibility leads to a vortex-deconfined regime for arbitrarily weak magnetoelectric coupling. The results provide insight into how intertwined superconducting and easy-plane ferromagnetic orders can reshape phase coherence, with relevance to rhombohedral graphene proximitized by a transition-metal dichalcogenide substrate.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the interplay between superconductivity and easy-plane ferromagnetism in 2D materials, showing that magnetic fluctuations induce a 'smectic' superconducting state. This state suppresses phase coherence by modifying the superfluid stiffness, leading to a finite vortex energy cost. The restoration of true order requires external pinning mechanisms, providing insight into superconducting phase transitions in magnetically coupled heterostructures.
main_problem: The paper investigates how soft nonunitary fluctuations of the pair condensate suppress phase coherence in a 2D Rashba superconductor near easy-plane ferromagnetic order.
main_result: This interaction drives the system into a 'smectic' superconducting state, destroying quasi-long-range order at finite temperatures unless weak lattice anisotropy pinning is present.
method: The analysis involves integrating out soft magnetic fluctuations to derive an effective free energy for the superconducting phase, leading to a smectic elasticity description.
model_or_system: The model is a 2D superconductor coupled to an easy-plane ferromagnet, relevant to rhombohedral graphene on a TMD substrate. The physics is governed by a magnetoelectric coupling term derived from a Lifshitz invariant.
key_observables: Superfluid stiffness ($ho_{x, eff}, ho_{y, eff}$), vortex energy cost, and the superconducting phase coherence temperature ($T_{	ext{BKT}}$).
important_parameters: Magnetoelectric coupling strength ($\lambda$), pinning strength ($\mu_\perp$), and the ratio of characteristic length scales ($\xi_{\lambda}$ vs $\xi_{\mu\perp}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on expanding the free energy around a magnetized saddle point and treating fluctuations perturbatively.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the effective Hamiltonian incorporating magnetoelectric coupling, deriving the smectic elasticity, analyzing the consequences for vortex energy, and finally discussing the restoration of order via pinning mechanisms.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent gauge fields and the resulting smectic phase transition provides a rich analogy for understanding phase coherence loss in coupled quantum systems, which is relevant to superconducting qubits or Josephson junction arrays.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Illustration of a vortex in a smectic superconductor. The color represents the superconducting phase. Through the magnetoelectric coupling, the spin polarization of the conden- sate acts as an emergent gauge field for the superconducting phase. The U(1) phase gradient is locked to the transverse nonunitary magnetization, displaying a helical texture with pitch 2π/|λm0|. In absence of in-plane pinning of the trans- verse fluctuations, a vortex defect (black) has finite energy cost and QLRO is destroyed. White arrows indicate the local in-plane magnetization, m(r).

FIG. 2. Phase diagrams for a Rashba superconductor co- existing with easy-plane ferromagnetism for magnetoelectric coupling (a) λ = 0 and (b) λ ̸= 0, as a function of tem- perature and phenomenological parameter, J. The ferromag- net is assumed to have an in-plane sixfold anisotropy. Dark blue denotes a uniform unitary superconductor, and the light and dark yellow phases denote the QLRO and LRO canted ferromagnetic (FM) phases, respectively. The solid red line denotes the BKT transition, and above, light shading indi- cates a vortex-deconfined regime. The solid black contour denotes Tm which describes the onset of QLRO FM, and the solid gray line, Tµ⊥, separates the QLRO FM from the LRO FM....
